reason: This text from 1 Samuel 28-30 does not support the statement. The passage shows contrasting treatment based on faithfulness rather than a general favoritism toward leaders over people: (1) Saul, a Hebrew leader, is harshly judged—Yahweh refuses to answer his inquiry and takes his kingdom away, showing Yahweh does NOT unconditionally care for leaders. (2) David, also a leader, receives empathy and help—Yahweh answers his prayer and assures him of victory and rescue. (3) The people are portrayed sympathetically in their suffering—David and his men weep greatly when their families are taken captive, and David is motivated to pursue the raiders. (4) Yahweh demonstrates empathy for the people by enabling David's successful rescue and recovery of the captives. The text shows differentiated divine treatment based on obedience/faithfulness (Saul vs. David), not categorical care for leaders over people. The people's suffering appears as a consequence of their leader's disobedience, not evidence of Yahweh's indifference to them.
